title: A DOM probe that returns 'not found' can be a selector-shape miss — check whether the creator assigns an id, attribute, or custom tag before concluding the feature never ran
trigger: An evaluate/querySelector probe reports the target missing while every other signal (sibling artifacts, suppressor styles, video state) says the feature initialized
principle: querySelector('X') matches TAG X, not id X. Verifying a mount marker by tag name when the code sets host.id = 'X' yields a permanent false negative that costs the whole debug session chasing phantom injection failures. Before trusting a not-found probe, grep the creation site for how the marker is emitted (id=, dataset, custom element tag) and probe exactly that.

cases.context: Onflix iframe: probing document.querySelector('Tihoka-subtitle-root') returned null for ~10 minutes of debugging while nativeHide:true and a playing video proved init ran — the host is created via host.id = 'Tihoka-subtitle-root' (an id attribute, not a tag).

applyFor: any mount/injection verification by DOM marker
extending probe scripts that assert on element existence
reading CSS/feature flags emitted as attributes vs elements
